danny.audio_profile: Danny, a regular guy in his late thirties. He is genuinely a little scared and still shaken, and he tells what happened plainly and honestly, in a natural voice with very little inflection, keeping his pitch fairly level and even, like a real person, not an actor.

marcus.audio_profile: Marcus, 22, a big, easygoing young man with a deep voice, talking low into his walkie-talkie.

scene: A man quietly tells what happened during the first hour of a zombie outbreak at the mall where he works. Close to the microphone, plain and natural, no music.
sample_context: A first-person story told plainly, in a natural, slightly scared voice.

chunks.text: I have a key to every store in this mall.
The man who gave them to me said never to use the last one.
I'm Danny. I'm the night guard at Maplecrest Mall.
I work nights so I can be at the bus stop at three-fifteen when my daughter Lily gets off.
We live with my mom, on the tenth floor of the Parkview Apartments, right across the highway.
Every night at nine, when I walk in to work, Lily blinks her lamp at the mall three times.
It means I love you. I blink my flashlight back.
I taught her one more signal, S-O-S, for emergencies. She thinks it's a game.
Forty-two keys. Old Walt had this job before me, and when he handed them over, he tapped the last one.
"That one, you never use," he said. "Don't ask."
Its tag says B3. There is no B3 on the mall map.
Tonight, I'd only need one of them.
In thirty days, I'd find out what the last one opens.
